transcript.answer: No. Setting a fallback model and passing `resilience` to HAL Engine is not enough. HAL Engine's `resilience` setting is only a retry policy and has no fallback field. HAL Engine fails over only through `fallbackProviders`. Before issue #474 and PR #475, `buildEngine` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` passed `createHalEngine` a `provider` and no `fallbackProviders`. `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` was validated against the allowlist and printed in the `api.model` startup line, but the engine never tried it. PR #475 fixed this by passing the resolved fallback as the only entry of `fallbackProviders`, and an empty list when `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` is unset. Only the mock model can currently be a fallback, because building a real fallback needs that vendor's own settings (KU-07). One spec scenario (User Story 3) still describes a `resilience.fallback.provider` block, so it may be stale. I did not check whether it was updated.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly says resilience is only a retry policy and failover needs fallbackProviders, but it claims only the mock model can currently be a fallback, while the gold says a mock fallback behind Vertex is refused.
